title: 1946 Australian National Airways DC-3 crash
summary: Australian National Airways Flight VH-AET departed Hobart on March 10, 1946, with 21 passengers and 3 pilots, one of whom was a supernumerary pilot on his first flights with the airline. The takeoff was normal with both engines operating perfectly. Reaching about 400 ft, the aircraft turned left and descended steeply. It crashed into Frederick Henry Bay less than 2 minutes after takeoff, after flying only 2.9 nautical miles.
probable_cause: The investigation panel concluded the most likely cause was that the automatic pilot was inadvertently engaged shortly after takeoff while the gyroscope was caged. A subsequent inquiry by a Supreme Court judge discovered the captain was diabetic and kept this secret from his employer and the aviation authority, considering this condition probably contributed significantly to the accident.

factors.evidence: panel was satisfied that autopilot was inadvertently engaged shortly after takeoff while the gyroscope was caged
captain was diabetic and had kept it secret, judge considered his diabetes and self-administration of insulin probably contributed significantly
operation of the automatic pilot on-off control was not distinctive from operation of any other control in the cockpit
aircraft achieved normal climb of about 325 feet per minute before suddenly commencing descent of about 17½%

events.text: The return flight to Essendon Airport did not depart until 8:50 pm.
Observers at the aerodrome reported that the takeoff was normal, and both engines were operating perfectly.
Witnesses in the vicinity of Seven-Mile Beach estimated that the aircraft reached a height of a little above 400 ft before turning left slightly and descending steeply.
The panel members were satisfied that, after take-off, VH-AET achieved a normal climb of about 325 feet per minute before suddenly commencing a descent of about 17½%.
The aircraft cleared the land and crashed into Frederick Henry Bay about 300 yd beyond the water's edge and a mile from the western end of Seven-Mile Beach.

notes: investigation panel could not conclusively establish cause, identified autopilot engagement as most likely
Supreme Court inquiry examined three theories but found insufficient evidence for any one
captain's secret diabetes added posthumous contributing factor discovered after initial inquiry
